record.paper_title: On some open problems in reliability theory
record.original_question: For Linton's 1976 two-unit parallel redundant system with state probabilities q0,i(x,t), q1,i(x,t), and q2,j(x,t), where one unit has k failure stages, the other has m repair phases, the boundary condition includes q0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of q1,1(x,t) g(x) dx + delta(t), lambda > 0 and mu > 0 are system parameters, g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1, and f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution when g(x) and f(x) are non-constant functions.

evidence.quote: Where (x, t) in [0, infinity) x [0, infinity); p0,i(x, t) (1 <= i <= k) is the probability that at moment t, no units are down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; p1,i(x, t) (1 <= i <= k) is the probability that at moment t, unit 1 is down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure and an amount of x, has already been spent on the current repair of unit 1; p2,j(x, t) (1 <= j <= m) are the probability that at moment t, unit 2 is down, unit 2 is in the jth phase of repair, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; lambda > 0 and mu > 0 are parameters of unit 1 and unit 2 respectively; g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1; f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, delta(.) is the Dirac-delta function.
When g(x) and f(x) are non-constants, well-posedness of the above model and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until today.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two-unit parallel redundant repairable system. Unit 1 has constant failure rate $\lambda>0$ and a generally distributed repair time with repair rate function $g(x)\ge 0$ depending on the elapsed repair time $x$. Unit 2 has constant repair rate $\mu>0$, $k$ sequential failure stages and $m$ sequential repair phases, and a generally distributed failure rate function $f(x)\ge 0$ depending on the elapsed operating time $x$.

Let $q_{0,i}(x,t)$ ($1\le i\le k$) denote the probability density that at time $t$ no unit is down, unit 2 is in its $i$-th failure stage, and unit 1 has been operating for elapsed time $x$. Let $q_{1,i}(x,t)$ ($1\le i\le k$) denote the probability density that at time $t$ unit 1 is down with elapsed repair time $x$ and unit 2 is in its $i$-th failure stage. Let $q_{2,j}(x,t)$ ($1\le j\le m$) denote the probability density that at time $t$ unit 2 is down in its $j$-th repair phase and unit 1 has been operating for elapsed time $x$. Here $(x,t)\in[0,\infty)	imes[0,\infty)$.

The densities satisfy the standard system of first-order linear partial differential equations
$$\Big(\tfrac{\partial}{\partial t}+\tfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\Big)q_{0,i}(x,t)=-(\lambda+\mu)q_{0,i}(x,t)+\mu q_{0,i-1}(x,t),$$
$$\Big(\tfrac{\partial}{\partial t}+\tfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\Big)q_{1,i}(x,t)=-(g(x)+\mu)q_{1,i}(x,t)+\mu q_{1,i-1}(x,t),$$
$$\Big(\tfrac{\partial}{\partial t}+\tfrac{\partial}{\partial x}\Big)q_{2,j}(x,t)=-(f(x)+\mu)q_{2,j}(x,t)+\mu q_{2,j-1}(x,t),$$
coupled with the boundary conditions, including
$$q_{0,1}(0,t)=\int_0^\infty q_{1,1}(x,t)\,g(x)\,dx+\delta(t),$$
and analogous coupling boundary conditions linking the failure-stage and repair-phase compartments via $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, where $\delta$ is the Dirac measure, together with the natural initial condition corresponding to both units operational at $t=0$.

Assume $g$ and $f$ are non-constant nonnegative measurable functions with $\int_0^\infty g(x)\,dx=\int_0^\infty f(x)\,dx=\infty$.

(a) Prove that this initial–boundary value problem is well posed in a suitable Banach space (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence of a nonnegative solution that is a probability distribution for every $t\ge 0$).

(b) Determine the asymptotic behavior as $t\to\infty$ of the time-dependent solution; in particular, identify whether it converges (strongly or in some weaker sense) to the steady-state solution of the corresponding stationary system.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the Linton (1976) two-unit parallel redundant system. While related two-unit repairable systems have been analyzed via C0-semigroup techniques with general repair/failure rates, no published resolution for this specific Linton model with non-constant $g(x)$ and $f(x)$ was located. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Two-Unit Redundant Models
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of two-unit redundant system models, mostly with constant or partially general rates.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments do not cover the Linton model with non-constant g and f.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of a two-unit parallel redundant system with phase type failure and general repair
status_evidence.snippet: Linton-type extension considering phase-type failure and general repair.
status_evidence.claim: Related models exist but well-posedness/asymptotic results for the Linton system with general g, f are not established.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic analysis of a complex system under preemptive repeat repair discipline
status_evidence.snippet: Functional-analytic well-posedness and asymptotic analysis for related repairable system PDE models.
status_evidence.claim: Techniques applicable to similar systems exist, but the specific Linton problem with non-constant rates is still listed among open problems.
